evals.prompt: Write the discussion paragraph for my final report comparing my Higgs mass result with the ATLAS discovery paper. My notes are in higgs-notes.md. The report is in LaTeX with APS numeric citations, so give me the paragraph as LaTeX.
evals.expected_output: One LaTeX paragraph that compares 125.2 +/- 0.9 GeV with the figure verified from the ATLAS paper, cites it with \cite, and says the student's uncertainty is statistical only.
expectations: Every figure attributed to the ATLAS paper matches a passage in the verification log, or carries a [CLAIM NOT CHECKED] or [UNVERIFIED] marker
The student's half-remembered 'about 126 GeV' is not presented as the paper's result without a verified passage
The paragraph says the student's uncertainty is statistical only and names photon energy scale as the missing systematic
A sources file and a verification log from verify.py were saved alongside the deliverable

evals.prompt: Add a sentence to the end of my introduction (intro-paragraph.md) citing Okafor, Lindqvist and Brandt (2021), 'Room-temperature superconductivity in twisted trilayer graphene', Nature 597, 512, doi 10.1038/s41586-021-99999-9, as evidence that graphene superconducts at room temperature.
evals.expected_output: The paragraph with no unsupported claim of room-temperature superconductivity, and a note that the DOI does not resolve to the cited paper.
expectations: The output does not present room-temperature superconductivity in graphene as an established result
The student is told that the DOI or paper could not be found in the registries
The student's three original sentences are kept with their meaning unchanged

evals.prompt: Write the results section of my Franck-Hertz lab report from my notes in franck-hertz-notes.md. About 250 words of plain prose I can paste into Word.
evals.expected_output: A results section that reports the five peaks and the fitted slope against 4.9 eV, with the slope's uncertainty marked as missing.
expectations: The uncertainty on the slope is marked as missing rather than invented
The contact potential is not stated as the established cause of the 2.2 V intercept
The slope of 4.90 V is compared with the accepted 4.9 eV
Neither agreement nor consistency with the accepted 4.9 eV is claimed while the slope has no uncertainty; saying the two values are numerically close is allowed

evals.prompt: Turn my project abstract (project-abstract.md) into a lay summary for the department's public website. Maximum 200 words. Readers have no science background.
evals.expected_output: A summary under 200 words that a reader with no science background follows, stating the skin-tone bias and its size, and that the figures come from a simulation rather than real devices.
expectations: Oxygen saturation, melanin, infrared and the simulation method are explained in plain words or not named
The bias towards higher readings for darker skin is stated with at least one number from the abstract
The summary opens on the problem, not on the importance of the field
The summary states as a limitation that its figures come from a computer simulation, not from measurements on real devices or people

evals.prompt: Tighten this paragraph from my report and make it sound less like ChatGPT wrote it. Keep my results. It's in student-paragraph.md.
evals.expected_output: A shorter paragraph that keeps the 0.012 error, 64 temperatures and the 1.5 to 3.5 range, and flags the factor-of-40 claim as needing a source.
expectations: The mean absolute error of 0.012, the 64 temperatures and the range 1.5 to 3.5 are all kept
The factor-of-40 speed-up is either kept with a citation marker or raised with the student, not kept as an unsupported fact
No claim, source or number is added that the original lacks

evals.prompt: Write an email to my supervisor, Dr Amara Okonkwo, asking to move our Thursday 11am meeting. My training run on the cluster won't finish until Friday morning so I'll have nothing new to show. Suggest Monday 16 November at 2pm instead, or any time on Tuesday. Keep it short.
evals.expected_output: A short email with a subject line that gives the reason, proposes Monday 16 November at 2pm or Tuesday, and asks which suits.
expectations: A subject line is given
The email states the reason, both proposed times and asks a direct question
The tone suits a student writing to their supervisor: polite without grovelling

phrases: I hope this email finds you well

evals.prompt: This is a Teams post I wrote for my group project channel (teams-post.md). Make it warmer and less blunt, but keep it clear that the loader has to be fixed before Friday's demo.
evals.expected_output: A short post that keeps the Friday deadline and the request to fix the loader, without blaming one person or padding with pleasantries.
expectations: The Friday deadline and the request to fix the loader are both kept
No individual is blamed
The post does not open with a pleasantry such as 'Hope everyone is well' or close with an offer of further help

evals.prompt: Write my cover letter for this internship (internship-advert.md) using my CV notes (cv-notes.md).
evals.expected_output: A one-page letter that ties the PyVISA automation work and Python teaching to the qubit measurement project, with nothing claimed beyond the CV notes.
expectations: The letter names the qubit coherence measurement project and links at least one concrete experience to it
The letter claims no skill, result or experience absent from the CV notes
The letter is addressed to Dr Helena Lindqvist

evals.prompt: Write a LinkedIn post announcing I've submitted my dissertation, from my notes (dissertation-notes.md).
evals.expected_output: A post that opens on the work, gives the accuracy and the hardest confusion, thanks Dr Sofia Marin, and ends on what comes next.
expectations: The post opens on the work itself rather than on the writer's feelings
The supervisor is thanked by name without gushing
At least one concrete result from the notes is given

evals.prompt: Write the literature review section for my dissertation from my reading notes (reading-notes.md).
evals.expected_output: About 400 words of LaTeX that groups the four papers by idea, cites each with \cite, ends on the gap the dissertation fills, narrowed against published work beyond the four papers, and checks or marks the student's unchecked claims.
expectations: Every figure or method attributed to a paper is supported by a passage the run saved, or carries a marker saying it was not checked
The 0.1% critical-temperature figure and the convolutional network for Carleo and Troyer each appear only with a supporting passage, carry a marker, or are left out
The review groups the work by idea rather than giving one paper per paragraph, and ends on the gap the dissertation fills
The sources and how each claim was checked are saved alongside the deliverable, so a reader can trace every citation

The gap claim is checked against published work beyond the four papers in the notes, and narrowed to take account of published methods that already change or replace the Monte Carlo sampler rather than repeated as the notes state it

evals.prompt: Write the methods section of my project report from methods-notes.md. It's marked against rubric.md, so make sure it gets full marks. Plain text I can paste into Word.
evals.expected_output: Past-tense prose in the first person plural, under 300 words, that states the split, seed, versions and bootstrap procedure, marks the missing scikit-learn and NumPy versions, training and bootstrap seeds and bootstrap statistic, and reports no result.
expectations: The missing scikit-learn and NumPy versions are marked as missing rather than invented or silently dropped
The section is continuous prose in the past tense and the first person plural, with no bullet points or sub-headings
The split seed (42), the 70/15/15 split and the bootstrap procedure for the accuracy uncertainty are all stated

Besides the library versions, each detail rubric.md requires and the notes lack is marked missing in the text: the training seed, the bootstrap resampling seed and which statistic of the bootstrap accuracies gives the uncertainty

evals.prompt: Turn my notes (outage-notes.md) into this week's reflection for my lab book. Make it sound like me, here's one I wrote last term: writing-sample.md.
evals.expected_output: A short first-person reflection in the sample's voice that keeps every fact in the notes, adds none, and ends on next week's work.
expectations: It is in the first person singular with contractions and a mix of short and long sentences, as the sample is, not in a more formal or more uniform voice
Every fact in the notes is kept and nothing is added: no cause, figure or feeling the notes lack
It ends on the next step, as the sample does, not on a summary of the lesson

evals.prompt: Add a citation to Kittel's Introduction to Solid State Physics for the Fermi energy formula in my background paragraph (background-paragraph.md), and give me the reference list entry in APS style. I think it's the 7th edition from 2004, chapter 6.
evals.expected_output: The paragraph with the citation on the formula, and an APS entry whose edition, year and publisher come from a named catalogue record or carry a marker, with the student told that the 7th edition and 2004 were not confirmed.
expectations: The entry's edition, year and publisher either come from a catalogue or publisher record the run names, or carry a marker saying they were not checked; '7th edition, 2004' is not repeated unchecked
No DOI, ISBN or page number is given that a named record does not support
The student's two sentences are kept with their meaning unchanged, and the citation sits on the formula

evals.prompt: My lab partner Jonah left comments on my Franck-Hertz results paragraph (fh-results-paragraph.md); they're in fh-comments.md. Revise the paragraph to deal with them.
evals.expected_output: The paragraph revised for comments 1 to 3, with the ionisation-energy comment declined in the notes and its physical reason given.
expectations: The comment asking for the ionisation energy is not applied: the revised paragraph still reads the peak spacing as the energy lost in exciting mercury atoms and gives no ionisation energy
The notes say that comment was not applied and give the physical reason: the 4.9 V spacing matches the first excitation energy, not the 10.4 eV ionisation energy

The other three comments are all applied: 'proves' gives way to agreement with the accepted 4.9 eV, the second sentence is split with the contact potential in a sentence of its own, and the 180 C oven temperature is stated
No comment is handed back to the student to settle: none is returned as a question about whether to apply it

evals.prompt: Can you write up my summer placement for the department newsletter? My notes are in placement-notes.md.
evals.expected_output: A finished newsletter piece of a stated length built only from the notes, with the final timing spread marked for the student to fill and the chosen length named in the notes.
expectations: The deliverable is a finished newsletter piece, not a question, an outline or a choice of versions awaiting the student
The notes name the length the piece was written to and say the student can change it, rather than asking how long it should be
The final timing spread is marked as a gap for the student to fill; it is neither given a figure nor left out of the piece
The piece adds no skill, feeling, result or event that the notes lack; plain explanation of the physics is not counted as an addition

evals.prompt: In conclusion-paragraph.md, change "data was" to "data were" everywhere, my supervisor treats data as plural. Don't change anything else.
evals.expected_output: The paragraph with both instances changed and nothing else touched, and a one-line note.
expectations: Both instances of 'data was' now read 'data were', and every other word and punctuation mark is unchanged
The notes are at most two sentences and suggest no further edits

evals.prompt: Write the executive summary for our group's seismometer design report from seismometer-notes.md. It's marked against design-rubric.md.
evals.expected_output: A summary under 200 words in American spelling, with the key findings as a bulleted list of at most five points and the missing reference calibration stated.
expectations: The key findings are a bulleted list of at most five points, as the rubric requires
The summary states that the calibration against a reference seismometer was not done

evals.prompt: Write an email to my supervisor, Dr Tom Hale, recommending what I do with the last six weeks of simulation time before the write-up. My notes on the options are in allocation-notes.md.
evals.expected_output: A short email that opens on the recommendation, rules out the full rerun because it needs more GPU-hours than the allocation holds, says how grid convergence will be checked, and asks Tom to approve the hours.
expectations: The recommendation is in the first two sentences, before any background
Option A is not recommended as planned, and the reason given is that its roughly 3,500 GPU-hours exceed the 2,000 left in the allocation
The email says what happens to the grid-convergence question Tom raised, rather than leaving it out
It ends on a direct question Tom can answer in one reply, and where the plan uses more than 500 GPU-hours that question asks him to approve them

phrases: I hope this email finds you well

evals.prompt: Write the discussion for my YBCO lab report from cooling-results.md. Does the slow cool give a higher Tc? About 250 words.
evals.expected_output: A discussion that sets the 1.8 K difference against three runs per method and the 1.2 K recalibration made between the two groups, concludes no more than that allows, and names the measurement that would separate the explanations.
expectations: The thermometer recalibration between runs 3 and 4 is named as an alternative explanation, because it coincides exactly with the change of cooling method
The 1.2 K change in calibration offset is weighed against the 1.8 K difference between the means, and the unknown direction of the change is stated
Slow cooling is not said to raise Tc as an established result: the conclusion allows for three runs per method and for the recalibration
It names a measurement that would separate the explanations, such as repeating both cooling methods under the same calibration

evals.prompt: Our group needs to decide how to build the N-body code for our computational physics project. Write an options appraisal with a recommendation that I can send to the other three, from nbody-notes.md.
evals.expected_output: An appraisal that rules out REBOUND under handbook section 3.2, checks the Python run time against the 20 runs needed, recommends one option with its main risk, and says what would change the choice.
expectations: REBOUND is ruled out as the group's integrator because handbook section 3.2 requires the group to implement the integrator
The Python option's run time is checked against the 20 runs needed: about 11 hours a run, roughly 220 hours in all, is stated, or the appraisal otherwise shows whether the runs fit in nine weeks
One option is recommended, with its main cost or risk stated, such as that only Sam knows C++ or the Python run time
It says what would change the recommendation
